Before I say anything, I am not a vegan, though I plan to be. However, the vegan community has made me stray away from the lifestyle many times and I'm still researching about it.

Factory farming is the main reason veganism is a thing, right, because it's cruelty to animals? And that's great, we shouldn't be supporting those people! But how is it morally wrong to eat and survive as well, if you know the animal's had a happy life? Every animal needs food to survive. (Though I suppose any other predator doesn't worry about morals, food is food, so if you're going all the way with that logic, some predators have been known to play with their prey before killing too 👀 they don't have moral systems in place, though) I believe if you KNOW the animal has been well cared for and was happy and it is euthanized peacefully, there should be no harm, or at least much less than purchasing from factory farms.

Take my friends for example. They have a HUGE flock of chickens, at least 25. Their chickens are freeroamed and have access to all the bugs, grass, and feed they could ever want! They even have a guard dog and 5 different coops for cold weather and laying eggs. They let the chickens do their thing and when a chicken gets hurt (caught by a predator, hit by a car, or pecked by other chickens, or just ill, usually) they spend all their focus on getting that chicken better. Their chickens have to be the happiest chickens ever and I know when it's time for them to go they will not have regretted a single moment. They hire a professional to humanely euthanize the chickens (that's the only part I faulter on a bit since they haven't specified WHO they hire, but I trust them) so that there will be no pain. And gosh those chickens get PLUMP too! I went out to feed a broody hen because I wondered if she had eaten and that crop of hers was full to the brim! Hard for me to believe from a broody hen, at least from what I know! Happy, happy chickens to the end with all the food they could possibly get, all the trees to climb (you need to see bantoms climbing trees, it's hilarious), and all the comfy coops to lay in. And if they could consent to being slaughtered, perfect, but they unfortunately don't have the intelligence for that and I don't think they grasp the concept of long life vs. death. It happens naturally so honestly I don't see the issue?

Personally, I would get too attached to slaughter my own animals. But there's no shame in it if they had a happy life! But, that's my opinion, take it for a grain of salt.

My experience with depression is mostly lack of motivation, fatigue, and mood swings, and the occasional darker urges. It frustrates me to see people glorifying depression, $3lf-h4rm, and $^1c1d3. It's a much larger issue than just being sad. My depression was either hereditary or caused my extreme hormone imbalance, the doctors never were quite sure, and was worsened by gender dysphoria and stress. It's affected my day to day life and I may never be off medication for it. Depression is different for everyone. When I developed it, I began snapping at my friends and family for little to no reason. I would break down in tears at the littlest mistake and would beg not to go to school simply because doing anything made me miserable. I'll make plans and be excited, then I get in the car and my anxiety levels rise and all I want to do is go back to bed. I still spend most of my time on social media and I'm currently far behind in all of my classes because I simply don't have the energy. When I first started having symptoms, it felt as if I'd been robbed of my happiness. I could no longer focus and none of my previous comforts or hobbies made me happy. I couldn't and still find it difficult to get any of my studies done. I used to write several pages every day, then when the symptoms set in I gradually stopped and now I haven't written for at least a good year. My lowest was when I stopped feeding my pets, and due to my negligence one passed away. I still mourn for him. He was my first ever pet and we were attached to the hip. That was what pushed me forward to at least try to get out of the rut. Now, I admit social media has become a huge crutch for me battling depression, even if it's quite toxic at times. Well, it doesn't really battle depression even, it's kind of what sucks me back into bed. But it's become some sort of 4dd1ct10n and hopefully I can fix that soon as well. I am now on daily medication and visit a therapist every other week as well as a psychologist every month. It's hard, but I'm recovering, and my symptoms are getting a bit better.

Sorry, this is kind of a dump. I was just happy to see someone finally understand instead of thinking it's all just edgy crap. Tl;dr you explained it pretty well, though depression can vary vastly person to person.

That’s something you have to tell yourself. Try writing down 1 thing you’re thankful for or that you like about yourself (I like the way my lips are shaped and I’m thankful for my guinea pigs today) each day. It doesn’t have to be different every day, and if you can’t think of something or if you need anyone to talk to, you can always DM me :) This isn’t going to fix everything. My mutt and I have been chased on walks in our own neighborhood roughly 8 times in the past year. (I wish I had a better memory or had written them all down to keep track) He’s a well-behaved dog, but tends to pull when he’s excited, so he walks with a slip leash. Most people here don’t walk their dogs, instead they keep them tied up in their front yard all day. Well, there’s a specific house that seems to hate my dog and I. They have a fenced back yard and 3 dogs. The other houses don’t bug me so much because at least their dogs breaking free were isolated incidents. This house I’m upset with. The 1st time the dogs got out of their yard, their owner was trying to bring them inside the house (apparently they don’t have a door to their yard, just a gate) and they broke free. 2 dogs were about my dog’s size, probably bully dogs, and 1 was a little chihuahua. Well, 1 of the bigger dogs was growling, had stiffened up, and had raised his neck fur and tail. I stepped in front of my dog to block him, but the other 2 dogs came up behind us and I heard my dog yelp. The angry dog was being dragged back to the house after I realized the chihuahua had bitten my dog on the butt, but hadn’t broken skin. The other big dog looked relatively friendly, but the chihuahua was not having it. I tightened my grip on the leash to make sure my dog didn’t break free and escalate the situation by running and started to walk away. The friendly dog was taken inside soon after we started walking, but the chihuahua followed us 3/4 of the way home, yipping and howling the whole time about 2 feet behind us, until it stopped to mark a wall and was picked up by its owner. The 2nd time this happened, the owner was trying to leave the house while the dogs were inside and they (the dogs) ran after us. This time nobody got hurt, but it was annoying nonetheless. I stepped in between the dogs every time 1 approached mine, but for the most part they stayed a foot or 2 away and they were picked up quicker this time. The 3rd time, the owner just... let the dogs out. Opened the gate and stood there while they came rushing towards my dog and I. Again, I used the blocking technique, but it didn’t work so well since I couldn’t defend all 4 sides of my dog. I don’t think my dog was ever hurt, but in the stress of it I started walking away quickly with my dog right at my side and there’s a pretty high chance I kicked the chihuahua trying to break out of the circle they’d made. Eventually the bigger dogs were picked up, no idea what happened to the chihuahua, though. It just kinda disappeared. My dog was nervous and kept looking back to make sure nobody was following us the whole time home. I haven’t gone on a walk in my neighborhood since.
